descriptionChirho: To know through personal experience, relationship, or acquaintance; general active-voice knowing encompassing all tenses, persons, numbers, and moods (present, aorist, perfect, future, imperfect indicative; subjunctive; imperative; infinitive; active participle) where the multilingual evidence does not disambiguate a more specific sense (Arabic عَرَفَ/عَلِمَ, Korean 알다, Swahili -jua, Spanish conocer/saber, Hindi जानना).

To grasp the meaning of something, to understand or comprehend, distinguished by Arabic فَهِمَ/تَفْهَمُ, Korean 깨닫다, Swahili -elewa/-fahamu, Hindi समझना, and Spanish entender rather than conocer/saber.
Ingressive sense: to come to know, learn, find out, or ascertain information not previously known; English 'finding out' / 'learned', indicating the moment of acquiring new knowledge.

Passive and middle-passive voice forms: to be known, be recognized, be made known, or become known; marked by Arabic مَعْروف/عُرِفَ/يُعرَفُ, Korean 알려지다/알려진, Swahili -julikana, and passive Spanish ser conocido.
Euphemistic sense denoting sexual intercourse, following LXX usage of γινώσκω for Hebrew ידע in the carnal sense (cf. Matt 1:25, Luke 1:34).
To recognize or acknowledge someone or something, often with a connotation of discerning identity or accepting authority; marked by Swahili -tambua and Hindi पहचानना where present in the gloss data.
